preamble: Devoicing of the voiced postalveolar affricate [dʒ] to its voiceless counterpart [tʃ] keeps place and manner and removes voicing. It arises mainly through final obstruent devoicing: in languages that have both affricates and neutralize voicing word-finally, /dʒ/ surfaces as [tʃ] at the end of a word or morpheme and reappears as [dʒ] before a vowel-initial suffix. Turkish and Catalan both show this alternation, and Turkish applied it to loanwords such as Arabic/Persian tāj 'crown' > taç.

examples.note: Turkish /b, d͡ʒ, d, ɟ, ɡ/ are devoiced word- and morpheme-finally and before a consonant; the spelling records the alternation as c ~ ç.

examples.from: Arabic/Persian tāj 'crown' (Turkish tac- [tɑːd͡ʒ] before vowel-initial suffixes, e.g. tacı)
examples.note: The loanword's final /dʒ/ was devoiced word-finally, giving nominative taç and plural taçlar against accusative tacı and genitive tacın.
The word goes back to Frankish *laiþ. The feminine keeps the voiced affricate between vowels; in the masculine it is word-final and devoiced.
Catalan final devoicing removes word-final /d͡ʒ/ from the surface, as in raig [ˈrat͡ʃ] and faig [ˈfat͡ʃ] 'I do'.
